caral-supe-civilization.name: Caral–Supe civilization
caral-supe-civilization.summary: A pre-Columbian society of coastal Peru with as many as thirty major settlements, flourishing from about 3500 to 1800 BCE and recognized as the oldest known civilization in the Americas.

altiplano-cundiboyacense.name: Altiplano Cundiboyacense
altiplano-cundiboyacense.summary: High plateau in the Eastern Cordillera of the Colombian Andes, the ancestral territory of the Muisca, averaging about 2,600 meters in elevation.

bogot-savanna.name: Bogotá savanna
bogot-savanna.summary: A high plateau in the Colombian Andes around modern Bogotá, home to the Muisca people, known for agriculture, emerald mining, and salt extraction.

lauricocha-culture.name: Lauricocha culture
lauricocha-culture.summary: An Andean preceramic culture in central Peru, about 8000 to 2500 BC, whose cave held some of the oldest human remains found in Peru along with early stone tools and rock art.

guitarrero-cave.name: Guitarrero Cave
guitarrero-cave.summary: A cave in the Callejón de Huaylas valley of Peru's Ancash region, standing high above the Santa River.

huaricanga.name: Huaricanga
huaricanga.summary: The earliest known city of Peru's Norte Chico civilization, established around 3500 BC in the Fortaleza Valley and considered the oldest city in the Americas.

hu-nuco.name: Huánuco
hu-nuco.summary: A city in central Peru, capital of the Huánuco Region, where the Higueras and Huallaga rivers meet.

chinchorro-culture.name: Chinchorro culture
chinchorro-culture.summary: A preceramic fishing culture on the coast of what is now northern Chile and southern Peru, lasting from about 7,000 to 1,500 BCE and famous for elaborate mummification; named a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2021.

za-a-valley-archaeology.name: Zaña Valley
za-a-valley-archaeology.summary: An archaeological area in northern Peru containing South America's earliest known irrigation canals, some dated to between 6,700 and 4,500 years ago.

sechin-bajo.name: Sechin Bajo
sechin-bajo.summary: An archaeological site in Peru with ruins dating from 3500 to 1300 BCE, home to one of the oldest known monumental structures in the Americas.

camarones-chile.name: Camarones
camarones-chile.summary: A small coastal commune in northern Chile, home to a fishing inlet and Chile's only Afro-Chilean community.

arica.name: Arica
arica.summary: Chile's northernmost port city, near the Peruvian border, an important trade outlet for landlocked Bolivia and site of ancient Chinchorro mummy finds.

olmecs.name: Olmecs
olmecs.summary: An early Mesoamerican civilization that flourished roughly 1200 to 400 BC in what is now Veracruz and Tabasco, known for colossal stone heads and considered one of the cradles of civilization.

caral.name: Caral
caral.summary: An archaeological site in Peru holding the remains of the Caral civilization's main city, about 5,000 years old and considered the oldest city in the Americas.

casma.name: Casma
casma.summary: A city on Peru's northern coast near the Casma and Sechín valleys, home to some of the largest prehistoric monuments in the world.

chinchorro-mummies.name: Chinchorro mummies
chinchorro-mummies.summary: Naturally and artificially preserved remains of the Chinchorro people, the oldest deliberately mummified bodies known, dating from about 5050 BCE; unlike many cultures, they mummified people of all ages and social status, not just elites.

lake-lauricocha.name: Lauricocha Lake
lake-lauricocha.summary: A lake in the Andes mountains of central Peru, near which a cave was found holding human remains about 9,500 years old, the oldest known in Peru.

paij-n-culture.name: Paiján culture
paij-n-culture.summary: An archaeological culture on Peru's northern coast dating to roughly 11,000 to 8,000 BCE, first described in the 1940s and known from dozens of open-air camps, workshops and stone quarries.

jequetepeque-river.name: Jequetepeque River
jequetepeque-river.summary: A river in northern Peru's La Libertad Region, north of the Chicama valley, whose fertile valley grows rice and holds Moche culture archaeological sites.

moche-river.name: Moche River
moche-river.summary: A river on Peru's northern Pacific coast running through the Moche Valley and the city of Trujillo.

valdivia-culture.name: Valdivia culture
valdivia-culture.summary: One of the oldest settled cultures in the Americas, thriving on Ecuador's Santa Elena peninsula between about 3500 and 1500 BCE.

santa-elena-peninsula.name: Santa Elena Peninsula
santa-elena-peninsula.summary: A peninsula in Ecuador holding the westernmost point of the mainland, a dry region with salt mines and an oil field, popular for whale watching.

chivateros.name: Chivateros
chivateros.summary: A prehistoric stone tool quarry and workshop near the mouth of the Chillón river northwest of Lima, Peru.

rafael-larco-hoyle.name: Rafael Larco Hoyle
rafael-larco-hoyle.summary: Peruvian archaeologist (1901–1966) who founded the Larco Museum in Lima in 1926 and developed the first academic chronology of Peru's pre-Columbian cultures.
